target_customer: Brands and consumers using Alexa and Google Assistant voice apps; also companies wanting voice design services
problem: Companies and developers lacked voice app expertise for the new Alexa and Google Home platforms; Opearlo built and designed voice apps.
business_model: Voice design agency plus a portfolio of consumer Alexa skills

founders.name: Oscar Merry
founders.background_notes: Amazon Alexa Champions page describes technical product management and engineering background, Alexa work since November 2015, and founder of the London Alexa Devs meetup in July 2016. No employers or education listed.

founders.name: Jess Williams
founders.background_notes: Per Voicebot she stepped away from voice apps after the sale.

technical_complexity.rationale: Alexa skills use Amazon's skill kit; hard parts were voice interaction design and quality, not infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Skills could be rebuilt by anyone on the same platform; the only asset was skill store ranking and reviews.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The platform owners controlled discovery and tooling; Opearlo's skills were sold to Matchbox.io in November 2019.

market_need_then: Alexa and Google Home launched in 2014 to 2016 and developers were building skills early; demand for paid voice work is not quantified in sources found.

branding.brand_signature: Find My Phone Alexa skill with over 24,000 reviews
branding.community_and_virality: Merry ran the London Alexa Devs meetup with 200 plus members per the Alexa Champions page.

brand_strength.rationale: The Find My Phone skill was well known in the Alexa store but the Opearlo name itself had little press.

outcome_analysis: Opearlo built about ten Alexa skills, one of which, Find My Phone, became a top rated productivity skill with over 24,000 reviews, but no funding amounts or revenue are public. In November 2019 Matchbox.io bought the company or its skills for undisclosed terms and one founder left voice apps, which suggests a small outcome tied to Amazon's platform. The causes are inferred, not stated by the company.
notes: Company website field is empty and no live site was found. Dealroom and CB Insights name Y Combinator and Catapult VC as investors with no amount or date; single aggregator sources, not recorded as a round. Voicebot says the company was bought while Dealroom says the skills were; reported as acquisition. Failure factors are my inference, no post-mortem exists. No dated 2017 competitor sources found. No source on name origin.
